fit: registered motor scale in a bioactivated glucoraphanin study with mustard-derived myrosinase identified in a linked formulation study
assessment: The linked laboratory study identifies white mustard as the source of processed myrosinase intended for this trial. The registry lists total UPDRS, no separate rest-tremor endpoint and no posted results. The actual clinical formulation remains unverified and the trial does not assign toasted seed separately.

fit: placebo-controlled mood proxies with oral Nepalese pepper extract in healthy adults
assessment: In 82 healthy adults, the acute contentment interaction had no clear between-arm contrast at any individual assessment. No clear chronic mood or anxiety difference was reported over 56 days. The lipid extract is a separate species preparation, with no clinical depression scale or Parkinson cohort.

fit: Sichuan pepper polyphenol extract with internally inconsistent mouse immobility reporting
assessment: The original Figure 2 bars for extract are above negative control, in agreement with Results and opposite to the Discussion's reading. Methods describe time until resting, and the graph gives only a generic time label. This result and the unaltered voluntary activity give no reliable direction for clinical depression from toasted pepper.

fit: coconut oil as an example in self-reported Parkinson OFF coping strategies
assessment: The Fox Insight survey included 2,110 respondents with OFF periods and 1,416 free-text coping responses. Coconut oil is one example in the six-response supplements category. No oil-specific count, processing grade, comparator or measured change in daily OFF time is reported.

fit: contrasting associations of serum carrot-associated carotenoids with sleepiness in general adults
assessment: In NHANES Table 4 Model 2, sleepiness factors were inversely associated with serum alpha-carotene and positively associated with beta-carotene. Other specifications were inconclusive. No raw carrot intervention, Parkinson cohort or separate Epworth estimate was involved.

fit: plant-rich and time-restricted nutrition with Epworth scores in people with Parkinson disease
assessment: The six-month trial's Table 2 shows Epworth means 6.65 to 6.5 in controls and 6.55 to 6.7 with personalized nutrition, with post-test p=1.000. The whole program had several components and the report supplies no carrot-specific intake or contrast.

fit: hoarseness during supervised whole roasted hazelnut challenges in children
assessment: Table 1 records hoarseness in three children during food challenges with finely ground roasted whole hazelnuts. The separate oil-body experiments used immunoblotting. The clinical study provides no cold-pressed edible-oil challenge, acoustic loudness measure or Parkinson cohort.

fit: dysarthria temporally associated with concentrated clove oil in one adult
assessment: One adult had dysarthria and weakness after an exposure to concentrated clove oil. The original case proposes toxicity without testing the oil and supplies no Parkinson diagnosis, culinary ground clove, or listener intelligibility comparison.

fit: dill as one odor in a post COVID smell-training trial
assessment: Forty post-COVID participants were allocated in a protocol that lists dill among 11 odor stimuli and measures smell. No posted results, separate dill arm, culinary leaf preparation, or ingestion were established.

fit: dizziness mentioned after oral cumin essential oil in an uncontrolled IBS series
assessment: The original mentions dizziness without count, posture, associated blood pressure or control. The abstract and Results give inconsistent enrollment counts. Concentrated essential oil and uncharacterized dizziness do not establish a ground cumin effect on Parkinson standing lightheadedness.

fit: mixed topical Sichuan pepper preparation and combined anxiety depression item
assessment: The recruiting pelvic-pain trial includes ground Sichuan pepper in a mixed plaster and EQ-5D as a secondary quality-of-life measure. It has no separate pepper arm, confirmed toasting, Parkinson cohort or posted results.

fit: sweet almond syrup and parent-rated inattention in pediatric ADHD
assessment: Inattention scores moved 11.57 to 6.20 versus 8.05 to 8.10 under placebo. Raw Tukey contrasts were p=.003 at baseline and p=.011 at week 12. The printed table does not clearly show a baseline-adjusted estimate. All children took methylphenidate and the syrup is a separate formulation from cold-pressed almond oil.

fit: corn oil comparator in a randomized human primary-insomnia trial
assessment: Among 30 analyzed, the ISI endpoint contrast was minus 1.9 points for CBD versus corn oil (95% CI minus 5.0 to 1.1). An objective sleep efficiency contrast favored CBD. Both arms used corn oil. The main and cognitive reports are one cohort. The registry dose and duration differ and refining is unreported.

fit: corn oil capsules as comparator in a 12-week sleep quality trial
assessment: Endpoint measured efficiency was 96.0% with DHA/EPA versus 93.7% with corn oil, p=.018. Subjective sleep initiation and maintenance had p=.351. The result is a fish-oil comparison in generally healthy adults and does not identify a corn oil effect, refining, or Parkinson insomnia.

fit: registered PSQI in randomized corn-oil exercise comparator trial
assessment: The registry registers the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Ethics code S61809 confirms the Dalle article belongs to the trial, but the complete primary paper and original seven-page supplement omit the PSQI outcome and registry has no posted results.

fit: same pharmaceutical grade corn-oil vehicle for both study groups
assessment: The primary drug report gives an actigraphy treatment difference and no clear pairwise subjective waking-often result. Both arms received the same pharmaceutical-grade oil. The comparison does not vary corn oil and does not involve Parkinson insomnia.

fit: sponsor reported sleep scale in a separate phase 2b corn oil comparator trial
assessment: The sponsor reports 355.4 versus 364.2 at endpoint for corn-oil placebo versus 1 mg drug (p=.24). The sleep-specific n and error-term definition are unavailable. No structured registry results, no Parkinson cohort and no oil-specific comparison.

fit: sleep quality registered for an energy-matched corn canola and fructose control
assessment: Older adults undergoing bed rest received a composite oil-and-fructose control or ketone monoester. Sleep quality and sleep disturbance were listed, with no registry results or separate oil assignment.

fit: registered PSQI and ESS in a corn-oil capsule comparator study
assessment: Daytime sleepiness and sleep quality are registered. The original Dretsch abstract is a plausible match, but the 60-day duration and corn-oil ethyl esters differ from the registered three-month oil capsules. Linked between-group sleep estimates and body access remain open.

fit: registered corn-oil comparator with linked sleep results retracted
assessment: The registry lists PSQI and ESS and shows no structured results. The linked reported results were retracted after data and analysis discrepancies. Registry narrative and repeats of the retracted publication supply no directional result.

fit: mashed potato and registered acute sleepiness in a pediatric crossover
assessment: A 22-child six-meal crossover registers a repeated sleepiness item. The plausibly linked primary abstract describes frozen and microwaved mash and supplies no item result. Boiling, full source linkage and exact sleepiness results remain unverified.

fit: potato chips compared with pistachios with daytime sleep related impairment
assessment: A recruiting study in midlife women compares potato chips and pistachios and registers daytime effects of sleepiness. No posted results, boiled potato, or Parkinson cohort.

fit: acute emotion inventory in a baked or fried potato protocol
assessment: The acute emotion measure includes sleepiness. This recruiting protocol uses baked and fried foods in adults without a Parkinson comparison. Boiled potato is absent.

fit: separate baked and fried potato meal protocol with sleep-related measures
assessment: The second REB experiment separately registers an acute sleepiness item plus next-morning sleep quality. The recruiting record provides no results, confirmed participant overlap or boiled potato assignment.
